t:
Which of the following parameters can be used by insurance companies as a trigger to detect fraudulent claims?

I. Excessive patients per doctor in hospital
II. Higher per patient average medical tests
III. Higher per patient average visit numbers
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
X has taken a Mediclaim policy from ABC Insurance Ltd. The policy states that if the insured visits any of the in-network hospitals, it will cover 90% of the expenses on occurrence of the event and 10% will be his co-pay. How will these type of policies help insurance companies?

I. Such mechanisms help to contain costs of insurer
II. It is a cost sharing mechanism used by insurance companies.
III. Such mechanisms are used to provide for higher spending being shared by the insured
e: Correct answer: I,II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: The risk of morbidity will be considered to be highest among ___________________.
e: Correct answer: Senior citizens (from the IC27 question bank).

t: A consumer can seek redressal at State Commission  if the value of goods  does not exceeds __________________.
e: Correct answer: Rs 1 crore (from the IC27 question bank).

t: ____________ show the total amount of claims paid and the corresponding number of claims for different years and the components of claim costs.
e: Correct answer: Claim analysis (from the IC27 question bank).

t: _____________ can show the amount of claim, the total amount paid and the amount paid for different benefits.
e: Correct answer: Claim analysis (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which of the following details of an applicant cannot form the basis for assessment of his/her health risks?
e: Correct answer: Name / ??? (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
In underwriting, the process of acceptance needs to be done with:-

I. Fairness
II. Inequitable basis
III. Without any prejudice
o: I,II and III / I, II ??? III
e: Correct answer: I and III / I ??? III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Under a standard health policy, the exclusion of a waiting period for making a claim would normally apply to which one of the following?
e: Correct answer: Hernia (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which major event took place in the year 1956?
o: Issuing of Life Insurance Corporation Act
e: Correct answer: Nationalisation of life insurance business (from the IC27 question bank).

t: If the cause of the loss is a peril insured against, the assured can recover the amount of the loss from the insurer. This is known as ____________________.
e: Correct answer: Principle of Proximate cause (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement with regard to hospital cash benefit scheme.

I. Hospital cash benefit scheme is available only for employees on standalone basis.
II. Hospital cash benefit scheme provides a daily allowance which is in addition to the indemnity claim and is unlinked to the actual expenditure incurred.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
Either I or II can be true
e: Correct answer: Only II is true (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Based on their year of introduction, arrange the following chronologically.

I. Central Government Health Scheme
II. General Insurance Corporation
III. Life Insurance Corporation
o: I, II and III / I, II ??? III
I, III and II / I, III ??? II
II, III and I / II, III ??? I
III, II and I / III, II ??? I
III, I and II / III, I ??? II
e: Correct answer: I, III and II / I, III ??? II (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Identify the medical conditions that have a high probability of future incidences of associated diseases of the heart, kidney and the nervous system.

I. Hypertension
II. Overweight
III. Raised sugar level
e: Correct answer: I,II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Health Insurance in India formally began with the ___.
o: Inception of the Employees State Insurance Scheme
e: Correct answer: Nationalisation of non-life insurance industry (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which of the following statements CORRECT with regard to Surplus share reinsurance?
o: The reinsurance contract is proportional to the or
A form of pro rata reinsurance indemnifying the ceding company against loss to the extent of the surplus insurance liability ceded on a share basis
A form of reinsurance that indemnifies the ceding
A structure where the reinsurer designs the entire
A structure  in which NGOs play the role of the di
e: Correct answer: A form of pro rata reinsurance indemnifying the ceding company against loss to the extent of the surplus insurance liability ceded on a share basis (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
For individual health insurance, information on which of the following enable an underwriter to determine the probability of future health problems that may require hospitalisation or surgical intervention?

I. Current health status
II. Personal medical history
III. Family medical history
e: Correct answer: I,II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Which of the following is a technology and process interface technique for detection of frauds in insurance sector?

I. Audits
II. RAG Analysis
III. Propensity Modeling
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: What is considered as domiciliary hospitalisation under Mediclaim?
o: It means that the patient is admitted to a hospita
It is that condition of the patient in which he cannot be moved to the hospital or if there is no bed available in any of the hospitals, then the treatment is taken at home
It is a special facility for the old and destitute
It means  hospitalisation is done only when certai
Treatment is given in the Ambulance to save life
e: Correct answer: It is that condition of the patient in which he cannot be moved to the hospital or if there is no bed available in any of the hospitals, then the treatment is taken at home (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement(s)

I. Hospitalisation indemnity products make good part or all of the losses incurred or amount spent during hospitalisation.
II. In insurance coverage on benefit basis, the amount that will be paid on the occurrence of a specified event is predetermined in the insurance policy and is not related to the actual expenditure incurred.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
Either I or II can be true
e: Correct answer: Both I and II are true (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Indemnity based hospital products:

I. Pay for all or a major part of the losses incurred or amount spent during hospitalisation
II. Pay a pre-determined amount on occurrence of a certain event
III. Covers the hospitalisation expenses for an individual up to the sum assured
e: Correct answer: I and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Mahesh Verma has a health insurance product, but the product does not bear many of the incidental costs associated with hospitalisation. He wishes to buy a product which covers incidental costs associated with hospitalisation. Suggest a product for him.
e: Correct answer: Daily hospital cash benefit (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Sub centres in hilly areas caters to ____ population size.
e: Correct answer: 3000 (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement

I. Genetic pre-disposition does not impact morbidity and need not be taken into consideration while accepting risk.
II. Stout, thin or average may be associated with morbidity in certain groups.
o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
Either I or II can be true
e: Correct answer: Only II is true (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Which of the following factors play an important role in deciding whether to buy/renew a health insurance plan?

I. Renewal rejected on flimsy grounds
II. Claim settlement takes long
III. Premium hiked in arbitrary manner
e: Correct answer: I, II, and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Pooja has taken a health insurance policy with a cover of Rs.2 lakh recently which has a clause for limits on usage of the following hospitalisation expenses: -

Room rent limit: 1% of the sum insured per day.
ICU charges: 2% of the sum per day insured subject to maximum of Rs. 10,000.
Doctor's fees: 3% of the sum insured per day Recently she was diagnosed with dengue and was admitted in the hospital for 4 days.

The total bill amounted to Rs. 50,000 and following charges were included in the bill:-

1. Room rent - Rs. 3,000/day = Rs. 12,000
2. Doctor's Fee - Rs. 2,000/ day = Rs. 8,000
3. Medicine Expenses - Rs. 13,000
4. Administrative expenses - Rs. 5,000
5. Monitor Charges - Rs. 4,000
6. Laboratory Charges - 8,000

What amount of her claim shall be reimbursed by the insurance Company?
e: Correct answer: Rs. 46,000 (from the IC27 question bank).

t: All of the following factors are considered  while pricing a health insurance product EXCEPT:-
o: The cost of administering the program such as issu
Customer behaviour such a fraud, renewal, cancellation of policies
The cost of marketing and distributing policies th
Companies need to cover their cost of capital and
e: Correct answer: Customer behaviour such a fraud, renewal, cancellation of policies (from the IC27 question bank).

t: The ancient text of "Dharmasastra" was written by ____.
e: Correct answer: Yagnavalkya (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Which of the following statements are false with respect to Liquidity risks associated with health insurance market?

I. The occurrence of this type of risk depends on the mix of investment options chosen by the insurer, as also the overall environment in the economy.
II. Underwriting practices and risk appetite of the insurer give rise to this type of risk
III. Even if the insurer is profitable, there can still be a mismatch between the cash flows, and current assets and liabilities.
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC27 question bank).

t: X has taken a top up cover from ABC Ltd. which provides coverage beyond the deductible amount of Rs 1 lakh chosen at the proposal stage. Which of the following health insurance product has been purchased by X?
e: Correct answer: High-deductible hospital indemnity covers / ????-? (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Prakash was diagnosed with lung cancer and admitted to the hospital for its treatment. He had a cashless insurance policy which was informed to the hospital. The hospital raised a medical bill of Rs. 10 lakhs. On an analysis of the bills, it was found that the bills were inflated by Rs. 2 lakhs. This is an example of which of the following?

I. Demand Side Moral Hazard
II. Supply Side Moral Hazard
III. Combined Moral Hazard
e: Correct answer: Only II (from the IC27 question bank).

t: In a contract both the parties are obliged to disclose all material information which may be of importance whether or not it is requested. This is known as _________________.
e: Correct answer: Principle of Utmost Good faith (from the IC27 question bank).

t: As per contribution clause, each insurer's share of the loss is based on _________________.
e: Correct answer: Rateable proportion basis (from the IC27 question bank).

t: X has a small family consisting of his wife and a 12 year old son. He has taken three Mediclaim policies, one for each member of his family, from a health insurance company for an individual cover of Rs. 1 lakh each. X was hospitalised due to heart attack and required surgery. The medical bill raised was Rs. 1.25 lakhs. How much amount will the insurance company be liable to pay?
o: Rs 1.25 lakh as there are 3 policies taken by X
Rs 1 lakh will be paid by insurer as per the plan coverage
Rs 50,000 as insurance company is liable to pay on
Rs 90,000 as insurance company is liable to pay on
No amount will be paid as X has been admitted due
e: Correct answer: Rs 1 lakh will be paid by insurer as per the plan coverage (from the IC27 question bank).

t: The health insurer collects an upfront contribution from an individual/investor and pools it over many people. Choose the term that best describes this contribution.
e: Correct answer: Premium / ???????? (from the IC27 question bank).

t: All of the following statement with regard to analysis of written premium are true EXCEPT:-
o: This analysis can show the number of people covere
This helps in identifying the average premium (on
It helps in calculating the unearned premium reserve at the end of the accounting period, which needs to be shown in the financial statements
This will help an insurer to understand where to f
This will help to monitor the result of rate actio
e: Correct answer: It helps in calculating the unearned premium reserve at the end of the accounting period, which needs to be shown in the financial statements (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
The diagnosis for myocardial infarction will be evidenced by which of the following criteria?

I. A history of typical clinical symptoms consistent with the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (for e.g. typical chest pain)
II. New characteristic electrocardiogram changes
III. Elevation of infarction specific enzymes, Troponins or other specific biochemical markers
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: X has taken a health insurance product from ABC Ltd. which offers to pay fixed daily allowance to insured, which could be used to cover the unexpected and incidental costs associated with hospitalisation such as travel and stay costs of an attendant. Which of the following health insurance product has been purchased by X?
e: Correct answer: Daily hospital cash benefit (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Insurance contract is a contract of utmost good faith where ______________.
o: It is voluntary on both parties to provide all inf
It is obligation only on the insured to provide al
It is obligation on both parties to provide all information which is material to the contract
It is obligation on the insurer to provide all inf
It is optional on both parties to provide all info
e: Correct answer: It is obligation on both parties to provide all information which is material to the contract (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which was the first Act enacted in the year 1912 to regulate the insurance companies in India?
o: The Indian Life Assurance Companies Act
e: Correct answer: The Indian Life Assurance Companies Act (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Business environment risk includes changes in exposure to:

I. Policy environment
II. Economic environment
III. Liquidity changes
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC27 question bank).

t: A consumer can seek redressal at District forum if the value of goods  does not exceeds __________________.
e: Correct answer: Rs 20 lakh (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
In which occupation/s is accident risk considered to be high?

I. Driver
II. Aviator
III. X-ray Machine operator
IV. Asbestos industry workers
e: Correct answer: I and II (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which of the following parameters in analysis is used to study the percentage of total claim amount paid for each claim range in proportion to the total claim amount paid?
e: Correct answer: Claim probability distribution (from the IC27 question bank).

t: Which of the following parameters ensures delivery of the promise undertaken by the insurance companies  towards quality service?
e: Correct answer: Customer centric service (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
In India, the public health system exists at which governmental level?

I. Central
II. State
III. Local
e: Correct answer: I, II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Personal accident policies are offered as:-

I. Standalone policies
II. Packaged product with other health insurance cover
III. Rider to life and non life products.
e: Correct answer: I,II and III (from the IC27 question bank).

t: In _______________, NGOs play the role of the distributor and "outsource" the design and administration of the entire insurance product to an insurance company who effectively acts as a reinsurer.
e: Correct answer: Social reinsurance (from the IC27 question bank).

t:
Identify the true statement.

I. Women are exposed to additional risk of morbidity during child bearing period.

o: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
Either I or II can be true
